requirements.evidence: app/Ops/DiscordOpsAlert.php:74 matches the contract `send(string $title, string $message, array $context = []): void`; no-op on null/'' at :76-80; `Http::timeout(5)->post($url, ['content' => ...])` at :83-84; key=value lines plus `mb_substr(..., 0, 1800)` at :102-108; sensitive-key regex `password|token|secret|authorization|api[_-]?key|webhook/i` at :67; Bearer redaction and recursive redaction of nested arrays rendered as JSON at :111-146; non-2xx and Throwable both logged with `Log::error` at :86-93, using a URL scrubbed by `scrub()` at :150-162. config/logging.php:173 makes `daily` the stack default and :181-187 adds the audit channel (daily, audit.log, info, 90). The `daily` channel is not changed in the diff, but LoggingConfigTest.php:5-10 asserts days=14. config/services.php:200-202 adds the key; .env.example:10-18 and phpunit.xml:27 pin LOG_STACK=daily; docs/ops/logging.md was added. No discord log channel exists.

conventions.evidence: Tests ship with the change (tests/Feature/Ops/*), CHANGELOG.md has entries under [Unreleased] Added/Changed, docs/ops/logging.md was added, and the public method has PHPDoc. The plain service class is what the task explicitly asks for, so it does not break the 'no service layers' rule. Small deviations: the Pest file declares a global `const WEBHOOK` and `function sentContent()` (DiscordOpsAlertTest.php:9,15), which leak into the global namespace shared by the test suite, and docs/README.md is not shown linking the new ops doc.

security.evidence: Webhook URL and its path are scrubbed from the exception message (DiscordOpsAlert.php:150-162). Only the status is logged on non-2xx (:87). Redaction applies recursively, and a sensitive key short-circuits before the array is inspected (:113-115). Stringable values go through the Bearer check (:131-133). No user-facing input surface or Livewire code is touched.

tests.evidence: DiscordOpsAlertTest.php covers: no-op for null and '' (:331-338), method/URL/JSON/exact content (:340-348), exact 1800-char multibyte truncation (:350-358), key, Bearer and nested redaction (:360-383), non-2xx logging without the token (:385-395), and a transport exception scrubbed of token and id (:397-408). LoggingConfigTest.php checks the daily, audit and stack configs and that there is no discord channel. Weak spot: 'audit channel accepts writes' (LoggingConfigTest.php:436-440) only asserts `expect(true)->toBeTrue()` and writes to the real storage/logs instead of faking or asserting the write.

simplicity.evidence: The class is compact and uses private constants, a small match-based `render()` and one recursive `redact()`. Slight extras: Stringable handling (:131-133) and the path-form scrub (:154-159) go beyond the spec. Both are defensive and cheap.

readability.evidence: Clear constant names (MAX_LENGTH, SENSITIVE_KEY, BEARER), small focused private methods (format/redact/render/scrub), a brief class docblock and comment, no dead code or debug output.

scope.evidence: Every file serves the task: .env.example, CHANGELOG.md, the notifier, logging/services config, docs/ops/logging.md, phpunit.xml and two test files. The notifier is not wired into jobs or handlers, which matches the out-of-scope list.

issues.explanation: The 'audit channel accepts writes' test asserts nothing meaningful (`expect(true)->toBeTrue()`) and writes a real file under storage/logs instead of verifying that the write lands on the audit channel.
Global `const WEBHOOK` and global `function sentContent()` in a Pest file pollute the global namespace and can collide with other test files (redeclaration fatal).
LOG_STACK is inserted between DB_CONNECTION and DB_DATABASE, which splits the DB env group.
Non-Stringable, non-JsonSerializable objects in the context render as `{}`. This is harmless but not documented.

review.summary: The change adds App\Ops\DiscordOpsAlert with config-driven no-op behaviour, key and Bearer redaction (recursive), multibyte-safe 1800-character truncation and a soft-fail path whose logs have the webhook URL scrubbed. It also adds the audit channel, makes daily the stack default, pins LOG_STACK in phpunit.xml, and updates the docs and CHANGELOG. Every requirement and contract item is met and tested. The remaining nits are a vacuous audit-write test and global helpers declared in a Pest file, so I would approve with nits.
